title: Template Score Explorer
description: The wake-word detector compares a window of features with an enrolled template. It first subtracts each band's mean over the window, so a steady offset does not matter; then divides by the length of what is left, so loudness does not matter; and finally takes the dot product with the template, which is already mean-subtracted and length 1. The score runs from -1 (the opposite pattern) to +1 (the same pattern).

learningObjectives: The learner will calculate the template score of 4 small windows by mean subtraction, unit normalization and a dot product, within 0.02 of the correct value in at least 3 of the 4.
prerequisites: feature, window, mean subtraction, unit normalization, dot product score, template (all defined in this chapter above the block).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: Why do W1 and W2 score the same even though W2 is twice as strong?
What does a score of -1 mean?
Why does the order of the frames matter?
commonMisconceptions: (1) A louder or stronger window scores higher. (2) A steady offset in a band changes the score. (3) A negative score means "no similarity" instead of "the opposite pattern". (4) The order of the frames does not matter.
assessmentOpportunities: Complete all four challenges. Mastery is 3 of 4 correct on the first attempt.
